name: pen_options
description: Polygon pen guides and raycast. Guides (world axis, right angle, straight line) are enabled only by the global snapping state and the global guide type bit, act only while DRAGGING a stroke point, never on the click that creates one, and are anchored on the dragged point's ring neighbours prev / next: world axes through prev / next (n >= 2), right angle in the plane perpendicular to prev - prevprev / next - nextnext (n >= 3), straight line along prev - prevprev / next - nextnext (n >= 4). The guide is applied to the quantised cursor. Raycast: a press on a stroke point hidden behind the background surface does not grab it (the press acts on empty space); it never places points on a surface.

provenance.notes: fresh worker per cell, NEW empty foreground mesh; top orthographic view, focus (0.07, 1, 0), 440 px per metre; global snap-type bits written per cell; one readback after the drop; vertices in click order

rig_ours.note: our test viewport cannot hold the guide cells at 440 px/m: 360 keeps the 0.005 m placement quantum (every target is a lattice value); the raycast cells keep 440; the focus stays on y = 1 and moves in x / z per group (in top view only its height is a term)

b8.strokes: 3-point cells click p0, p1 and press p2 at (0.2, 0.8), dragging it to the target; 4-point cells click p0, p1, p2 = (0.2, -0.3) and press p3 at (0.2, 0.8)
b8.drag_target_note: the drag ends on the pixel of the QUANTISED cursor (the not-engaged twin's readback, or the lattice point of the rounded raw for the 8 px cell): the recorded raw pointer is about 1 px off

b8_click.law: the guide bit on, the third point CLICKED at the guided cell's target: unguided

b9.setup: unit sphere (64 x 32 segments, radius 1, centre (0, 1, 0)) in a BACKGROUND layer; constraint off

occluded_press_raycast_on.law: p0 unchanged (0.3,1,0.2); a new point appears at the press and is dragged

click_over_background_raycast_on.law: clicks and the drag stay on the plane (y 1.0): raycast does not place onto the background

click_over_foreground_raycast_on.law: second stroke stays on the plane (y 1.0) over a slanted foreground quad

b9.description: press on p0's pixel and drag +40 px in screen x (occluded cells); the background / foreground cells press p1 and drag it to (0.5, 0.5) / (0.4, 0.5)

Gnext_a_line.law: next-side straight-line guide engages (dragged p0 on the line p2->p1 beyond p1; foot 1.5 mm from the projection of the quantised cursor)

Gnext_b_rightangle.law: next-side right-angle guide engages (= projection of the quantised cursor, exact)

Gnext_c_worldX.law: world-axis guide through the NEXT neighbour engages (exact)

Rfront_visible_point.law: raycast 1: a press on a VISIBLE point above the background surface grabs it (moved to the drag end, its height kept)

R4b_hidden_press.law: raycast 1, press on a hidden point: the panel holds 4 points [p0,p1,p2,new], current 3 (typed Current 0..4; 4 clamps to 3); the committed polygon is [p0,p1,new] (p2 left out) -- reproduced 3/3 (K-B2 R4, run2, clean run3); not explained

k_b3.description: Gnext: clicks p0 (-0.6,-0.4), p1 (0.2,-0.6), p2 (0.5,0.3), p3 (-0.3,0.5), then p0 dragged to the quantised cursor; Rfront / R4b: the B9 sphere and clicks, raycast on, snapping off
